description: The bar chart illustrates the performance ratio (in percentage) of three large language models—Llama3 (blue), Qwen2 (red), and ChatGPT (yellow)—across three distinct knowledge domains: Movies, Songs, and Basketball. The vertical axis represents the “Ratio (%)” ranging from 50% to 80%, with tick marks at 50, 60, 70, and 80. The horizontal axis categorizes the domains, with each domain displaying three adjacent bars corresponding to the three models. In the “Movies” category, Llama3 and Qwen2 both achieve approximately 85%, while ChatGPT scores around 73%. In “Songs,” Qwen2 leads at about 86%, followed by Llama3 at 84%, and ChatGPT at 62%. In “Basketball,” Llama3 scores around 67%, ChatGPT approximately 61%, and Qwen2 trails at about 57%. The chart visually suggests that Qwen2 performs best in Songs, Llama3 is most consistent across domains, and ChatGPT shows the lowest performance in Songs and Basketball. The gray square in the legend appears to be a placeholder or error, as no gray bars are present in the chart. The data reflects how model performance varies by domain, potentially indicating how knowledge popularity or domain-specific training affects LLM capability, as suggested by the paper’s title.
